user.title: Add a PTLevel receiver
user.description: Enter the address of a PTLevel WiFi receiver on your network. Receivers do not announce themselves, so give each one a DHCP reservation first.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the receiver.

reconfigure.title: Change the receiver's address
reconfigure.description: Enter the receiver's new address. It must be the same receiver; to add a different one, add a new entry instead.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the receiver.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach a PTLevel receiver at that address.
error.invalid_host: Enter just a hostname or IP address, without http://, a port or a path.
error.unsupported_receiver: Something answered at that address, but not a supported PTLevel receiver. Only Version 1 receivers (firmware 2xx, no button on the front) are supported so far.

abort.wrong_device: That address answers as a different receiver. To add it, add a new entry instead.

init.title: Tank level
init.description: The water column is measured from the chamber's air pocket, a few inches above the tank floor. Calibrate against a measured depth to get the tank's water depth, then set the full depth in Tank settings to get a percentage.

calibrate.title: Calibrate from a measured depth
calibrate.description: The receiver's latest report, at {reported}, shows {water_column} {unit} of water above the chamber. With this form open, press the transmitter's button and watch its light: if it does not show that the report went out, press again. Then measure the water from the tank floor to the surface straight away, while no water is being drawn or pumped in, enter the depth and submit. Submitting looks for the report your button press sent, and shows it with the resulting offset for you to confirm before anything is saved.

data_description.measured_depth: Water from the tank floor to the surface ({unit}).

calibrate_confirm.title: Confirm the calibration
calibrate_confirm.description: The report at {reported} shows {water_column} {unit} of water above the chamber. You measured {measured_depth} {unit}, so the depth offset will be {offset} {unit}.

tank.title: Tank settings
tank.description: Water depth is the water column plus the depth offset, and Percent full is the water depth as a share of the full depth. With a capacity as well, Water volume is that capacity scaled by the water depth, which suits any tank with straight vertical walls. Every tank sensor needs a depth offset: clear it to remove them all, or clear the full depth or capacity to remove only what depends on it. The chamber cannot sense water below its own air pocket, so the lowest reading means at or below the chamber. Lengths use {unit} and volumes use {volume_unit}, the units Home Assistant uses for your unit system.

data_description.depth_offset: How much to add to the water column to get the water depth: about the height of the chamber's air pocket above the floor. Calibrating sets it for you.
data_description.full_depth: Water depth that counts as 100%. Use the level where the fill pump stops, or the overflow if nothing stops the fill.
data_description.capacity: How much the tank holds when the water is at the full depth. A nameplate capacity is often measured to the brim, so start from your best estimate and adjust it until Water volume looks right.

error.cannot_read: Could not read the receiver just now. Your button press still counts: submit again in a moment.
error.implausible_depth: That measurement is too far from the reading to be right. Check the measurement, and that the transmitter has reported since the chamber went in.
error.low_reading: The new report shows almost no water above the chamber (under 1 inch, about 25 mm), which looks the same as a chamber out of the water or a leaking air tube. Check the chamber and its tube, press the button again, and resubmit.
error.no_new_report: No new report has reached the receiver since this form opened. Press the transmitter's button again, check that its light shows the report went out, wait a few seconds, and submit again.

abort.no_reading: There is no report to start from yet. Press the transmitter's button and wait a minute for the report to reach the receiver, then open Calibrate again and follow its steps; you will press the button once more after the form opens.
abort.not_loaded: The receiver is not connected right now, so there is no current reading to calibrate against. Once Home Assistant can reach it, open Calibrate again; you will need to press the transmitter's button after the form opens.
abort.unverified_scale: This transmitter's hardware has no verified pressure scale, so there is no water column to calibrate against. Water depth and percent full need transmitter hardware 16.
